title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers

content.text: BERT is designed to pre- train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers

**Core innovation:** Bidirectional context conditioning  
- Solves unidirectional limitation (e.g., OpenAI GPT)  
- Enables deeper context fusion across layers  
- Allows fine-tuning with minimal task-specific architecture changes  
**Impact:** Foundation for SOTA results across NLP tasks

content.text: BERT alleviates the previously mentioned unidi- rectionality constraint by using a “masked lan- guage model” (MLM) pre-training objective, in- spired by the Cloze task (Taylor, 1953). The masked language model randomly masks some of the tokens from the input, and the objective is to predict the original vocabulary id of the masked
word based only on its context.
This is also in contrast to Peters et al. (2018a), which uses a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LMs.
Dur- ing pre-training, the model is trained on unlabeled data over different pre-training tasks.
For fine- tuning, the BERT model is first initialized with the pre-trained parameters, and all of the param- eters are fine-tuned using labeled data from the downstream tasks.
In this work, we denote the number of layers (i.e., Transformer blocks) as L, the hidden size as H, and the number of self-attention heads as A.3
In order to train a deep bidirectional representa- tion, we simply mask some percentage of the input tokens at random, and then predict those masked tokens

BERT di base non sa cosa sia una risposta o una domanda. Per questo, durante il fine-tuning, gli scienziati "incollano" sopra BERT due vettori di numeri casuali, chiamati \(S\) (Start) ed \(E\) (End).

Questi due vettori sono come due fari da ricerca o "modelli ideali":

  • Il vettore \(S\) rappresenta l'identikit matematico di come dovrebbe apparire il vettore di una parola che inizia una risposta.

  • Il vettore \(E\) rappresenta l'identikit di una parola che finisce una risposta.
